summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: One synthetic field note (for Rover Beta, not Rover Alpha) reports intermittent J12 disconnects under vibration; no measurements, part data or pin mapping exist, so neither retention nor replacement can be justified yet.

sourceRegister.name: Field observation note — Rover Beta J12 (synthetic)

anchors.excerpt: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. This note is invented for demonstration. It is not a real field report.
Rover Beta, Robotics & Industrial demonstration unit.
An operator reported two intermittent J12 connector disconnects during a vibration run.
The drive controller lost its sensor-harness link briefly and recovered.
No measurement, vibration profile, retention value, pin mapping or board revision is recorded in this note.
No other document accompanies this note.

knownFacts.statement: The only source is a synthetic fixture invented for demonstration, not a real field report.
An operator reported two intermittent J12 connector disconnects during a vibration run.
The drive controller lost its sensor-harness link briefly and recovered.
The note records no measurement, vibration profile, retention value, pin mapping or board revision.
The note concerns Rover Beta, whereas the request names Rover Alpha.
No other document accompanies the note.

alternatives.title: Retain and investigate current J12 connector
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 connector and investigate the root cause (mating, retention, harness strain, crimp) of the reported vibration disconnects. Effectiveness is unknown until evidenced.
prerequisites: Identify current J12 part and board revision
Define vibration profile and reproduce the disconnect

alternatives.title: Evaluate a pin-compatible replacement connector
alternatives.description: Evaluate a replacement connector that preserves the board pinout. No candidate is named; compatibility is unknown until footprint, pin mapping and retention evidence exist.
prerequisites: Documented current J12 pin mapping and footprint

reviewQuestions.question: Does the Rover Beta observation apply to Rover Alpha's J12 hardware?
What is the current J12 part number, pin mapping and board revision?
What vibration profile and retention requirement must J12 meet?
Can the disconnect be reproduced and root-caused (connector vs harness vs crimp) under controlled vibration?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Defined profile and instrumented test setup

nextAction.action: Collect the current J12 baseline: part identity, pin mapping and board revision for Rover Alpha.

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
